newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight stays at 5.80 pct on bank lending.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight stays at 5.80 pct on bank lending.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate remained at 5.80 percent on Wednesday on continued lending by big local banks as well as foreign banks, dealers said.
"Most banks, local and foreign, are long and this is driving short-end rates lower," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank. "The overnight should stay below six percent."
There has been speculation the central bank, through its agent banks, has been supporting the overnight from falling below its perceived floor of 5.80 percent.
Dealers said players borrowing at the far end of the yield curve on concerns over the Thai baht, were lending aggressively at the short-end.
Earlier, one-week money fell to 6.60/70 percent against 7.20 percent on Tuesday.
One-month money was at 7.40 percent from 7.55, and three-month at 7.55 percent against 7.60.
The fall in rates on Wednesday came on the back of maturity of a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue which further improved market liquidity.
Bank Negara bills worth 1.5 billion ringgit had matured last week. The central bank has not announced any new issue to roll-over the maturities.
Dealers said the focus will be on whether a Bank Negara lending maturity on Thursday, said to be for two billion ringgit, will bring rates back up again.
"It all depends on what Bank Negara will do with the money. If the funds are channelled back into the system, then rates should remain under pressure," said one dealer.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were little changed as players were cautious while monitoring movements in dollar/ringgit, futures market dealers said.
The ringgit weakened above the 2.5200 a dollar level on Wednesday but no central bank presence was detected.
Futures rose earlier on the softening of interbank rates in the cash market.
At 0900 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) September contract was unchanged at 92.56, or an implied yield of 7.44 percent.
The December contract was up one point to 92.67, or 7.33 percent and March 1998 unchanged 92.74, or 7.26 percent.
